title: The integrated gate cannot see a CI workflow that names a deleted package
description:
From the ticks pwp run, 2026-09-15.

.github/workflows/ci.yml named ./internal/herd/collect/..., a package the epic deleted. The go job failed on every push and pull_request, so the epic's PR could never go green and the close-out rule that requires green CI was unsatisfiable. FIVE integrated gates passed over it.

Why the gate is blind to this: the gate runs the commands in [evidence.commands]/[testing.commands], which for this repo is 'go test -short ./...'. That pattern compiles only what EXISTS, so a stale path in a workflow file is not expressible as a failure. The workflow's own named-package step is never re-run by the gate, and nothing else reads the workflow at all.

The general shape: the gate proves the TREE is good, and says nothing about whether the repo's own CI configuration still describes that tree. Any config naming paths — a workflow, a codeowners file, a lint include list, a release manifest — can rot invisibly behind a green gate.

Options to weigh (do not assume the first):
- Have the gate parse workflow files for package patterns and assert each resolves. Cheap, catches this exact class, no new dependency.
- Have the gate run the repo's workflow steps directly (act, or a parsed runner). Expensive and duplicates CI.
- Declare it out of scope and require the close-out to check CI status on the PR instead, which makes it a human gate rather than a mechanical one.

Whichever is chosen, record why the others were rejected.

acceptance_criteria: A workflow file naming a path that does not exist in the tree fails the integrated gate, proven by a test that adds such a path and asserts the gate refuses; or the decision not to cover it is recorded with its consequence and the close-out check that replaces it
